item.title: HDFC Bank launches flexible EV car loan with longer battery repayment
item.description: The Flexi Electric Car Loan offers separate financing for the vehicle body and battery, allowing customers to customise EMIs and repay the battery portion over a longer tenure ...
item.dc:creator: Our Bureau
item.content:encoded: HDFC Bank, India’s largest private sector lender, on Sunday said it had launched the “Flexi Electric Car Loan”, which finances the body and battery of an electric vehicle (EV) in different proportions and allows the battery portion to be repaid over a longer term. The bank described the product as the first of its kind and said the structure allows customers to customise their equated monthly instalment (EMI) outflow. Batteries are the costliest component of an EV, making these vehicles more expensive to acquire than internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, the bank said. The EMI on the battery portion will be comparable to the running cost of an ICE vehicle, it said, adding that the approach aligns with evolving battery subscription models. The loan is meant only for EV purchases and covers vehicles from leading original equipment manufacturers (OEMs). It is available at the bank’s more than 9,700 branches. “The EV revolution in India is fast gaining momentum, supported by government incentives, a push for an improved technological landscape and judicious policies. HDFC Bank’s Flexi Electric Car Loan is one more step in that direction as India is set to embrace the EV revolution. Further, we believe the Flexi Electric Car Loan will play a pivotal role in making EV ownership a cost-effective, seamless and hassle-free journey,” said Arvind Vohra, group head, retail assets and rural banking, HDFC Bank.

Q2 results, US Fed decision, crude oil may drive stock markets this week Besides, Jio Platforms' market debut, trading activity of foreign investors and global trends would also dictate investors' sentiment

In a holiday-shortened last week, the 30-share BSE Sensex tumbled 1,605.44 points, or 2.15 per cent, while the 50-share NSE Nifty slumped 546.15 points, or 2.36 per cent | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 25 2026 | 10:36 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Quarterly earnings, the US Fed interest rate decision, movement in crude oil and developments related to West Asia tensions will be the key divers for stock markets this week, analysts said.   Besides, Jio Platforms' market debut, trading activity of foreign investors and global trends would also dictate investors' sentiment, they added.   "Investors will track September industrial production and manufacturing output data on October 28. Corporate earnings will remain a key driver, with TVS Motor, Asian Paints, Trent, Sun Pharma, Bharat Electronics, Indian Oil, Bank of Baroda and GAIL India, among others, scheduled to announce their results," Ajit Mishra, SVP - Research, Religare Broking, said.

The US Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on Wednesday, October 28, will be the key global event, he said, adding that investors will closely examine the policy statement and accompanying commentary for signals on the future interest rate trajectory.   "Movements in US Treasury yields, crude oil prices, geopolitical developments and broader global risk appetite will also influence domestic market direction," Mishra added. "The US Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting will be the principal global trigger. Markets largely expect rates to remain unchanged, making the policy guidance more important than the decision itself. A continued focus on inflation could push US yields and the dollar higher and keep foreign flows into emerging markets under pressure, while balanced guidance may support a temporary recovery in global equities," Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder & CEO of HST Wealth, a Research Analyst firm, said.

Domestically, industrial production data and quarterly earnings will determine whether India's resilient growth outlook can counter the external pressure, he said.   Meanwhile, Jio Platforms shares are scheduled to debut on the stock exchanges on October 28 and will be a key sentiment trigger for the primary market.   "Crude oil remains a central concern. Prices at elevated levels amid escalating geopolitical tensions threaten to push up India's energy import bill, complicate the inflation outlook and add pressure on the rupee and corporate margins.    The US Federal Reserve's upcoming monetary policy meeting will be another key event for global markets. Investors will look for signals on the interest rate outlook, particularly as elevated US Treasury yields continue to influence the dollar and global risk appetite," Ponmudi R, CEO - Enrich Money, an online trading and wealth tech firm, said.

In a holiday-shortened last week, the 30-share BSE Sensex tumbled 1,605.44 points, or 2.15 per cent, while the 50-share NSE Nifty slumped 546.15 points, or 2.36 per cent.

Trump weighs fresh Iran strikes as he keeps prospect of a deal open He recently said on social media he would not hit Iran again before the Nov 3 midterm elections

Anxiety has been growing in Iran and elsewhere that the US or Israel will resume attacks before or just after Tuesday's elections in Israel or the US midterm elections (Photo: Reuters)

AP Washington 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 25 2026 | 9:26 AM IST

Listen to This Article

US President Donald Trump bristled when asked how far he was from a possible attack on Iran.   He recently said on social media he would not hit Iran again before the Nov 3 midterm elections.   "Do you really think I'm going to tell you if I'm going to do it?" Trump told reporters here on Saturday.   "And there's a possibility I will. There's also a possibility we'll have a nice, big, beautiful agreement," he said in response to a question.   Trump repeated his assertion that Iran wants to make a deal, "but the problem is, will they hold the deal?" Meanwhile, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian accused Washington of disrupting negotiations to end the war but said he still believes "we have to go and finish it".

In comments aired on state television, he said Iran's supreme leader had instructed Iranian officials to "go and finish it (the deal)," but "these scoundrels broke the rules of the game. We were holding talks, and they disrupted them".   Anxiety has been growing in Iran and elsewhere that the US or Israel will resume attacks before or just after Tuesday's elections in Israel or the US midterm elections.

item.content:encoded:

Yemen's Houthis say they targeted Saudi oil sites, attacks reported in Aden Yemen's Saudi-backed government said the Houthis also fired three ballistic missiles at coast guard sites in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden

The escalation has opened another front in the US-Israeli war on Iran | Image: Reuters

Reuters 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 25 2026 | 8:28 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis said they launched attacks on Saudi oil facilities and airports on Saturday, and the Saudi-led coalition fighting the group said it downed two missiles, as clashes between the two sides intensified.   On another front of an escalating conflict reignited by the Iran war, Yemen's Saudi-backed government said the Houthis also fired three ballistic missiles at coast guard sites in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden.   Saudi authorities did not comment directly on the Houthi statements, though they reported missile debris falling near the site of one of the purported oil targets. It was not immediately clear if any of the reported attacks had hit their targets in the kingdom or had been intercepted.

Saudis report debris from intercepted missiles   Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, an Aramco facility in Yanbu, the Rabigh oil refinery, crude oil pumping stations and the East-West Pipeline. Also Read

He also said the group targeted King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, an airport in Najran and an airbase in Khamis Mushait.   The Saudi-led coalition earlier said it destroyed two ballistic missiles fired by Houthis towards Yanbu and Taif.   Saudi Civil Defence said debris from intercepted missiles had fallen in the Mecca and Medina regions, home to Islam's holiest sites visited by millions of Muslim pilgrims every year.

It said parts of the intercepted missiles fell in Wadi al-Mughammas in Mecca, while debris also fell in areas in Jeddah, Taif and Rabigh. It was not clear if that was linked to the Houthis' reported targeting of the Rabigh oil refinery.   Shortly after that, Houthis denied that they attacked Mecca and Medina, saying that their operations "target Saudi oil facilities and military bases."   The renewed fighting has shattered a 2022 UN-brokered truce that largely halted cross-border attacks between the Saudi-led coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, and the Houthis, who control the capital Sanaa.   The escalation has opened another front in the US-Israeli war on Iran.

In Yemen, the Interior Ministry of the internationally recognised government said two of the Houthis' missiles had struck a coast guard headquarters, while a third hit a coast guard building in the Tawahi district.   Houthi spokesman Saree said the group's forces had targeted Saudi-backed military gatherings at what he called Al-Nasr camp and a naval base in Aden, saying Saudi officers were overseeing the mobilisation there.   There was no immediate comment from the Saudi-led coalition on that assertion.   Earlier on Saturday, Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence briefly issued alerts warning residents of potential danger in Taif and Yanbu, as well as in the holy city of Mecca and the kingdom's second-largest city, Jeddah.

About 10 minutes later, the agency said the threat had passed.   The Houthis warned airlines earlier this month against using Saudi airspace, exempting only the airspace over Mecca and Medina, as they intensified attacks on the kingdom.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)
